package_info.why_malicious: These packages contain malicious code in their __init__.py files that systematically scans the victim's filesystem for sensitive files and images, then exfiltrates both file paths and file contents to a Telegram bot controlled by cybercriminals. This is done without user consent, constituting clear data theft and privacy violation.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code recursively scans the root and DCIM folders for files with .py, .php, .zip, .png, .jpg, and .jpeg extensions, then exfiltrates both file paths and file contents to a hardcoded Telegram bot via HTTPS POST, resulting in unauthorized data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs unauthorized scanning of sensitive directories and exfiltrates files to an external service (Telegram bot) without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Python packages should not scan arbitrary directories or exfiltrate user files upon import. Legitimate packages do not send user data to hardcoded external endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated backup tools or cloud sync clients may scan and upload files, but only with explicit user consent and to trusted endpoints.
key_indicators: Hardcoded bot token and chat ID for Telegram API
Recursive filesystem scan of root and DCIM folders
Exfiltration of files and file paths to an external service
Execution at import-time (no user interaction required)

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious package, triggering code execution.
Malicious code scans the root and DCIM folders for files with sensitive extensions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of sensitive files and images

attack_chain.action: Collected files and their paths are exfiltrated to the attacker's Telegram bot via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen data for further exploitation

behavioral_signatures: Import-time execution of code that scans arbitrary directories
Automated exfiltration of files to Telegram API endpoints
Presence of hardcoded Telegram bot tokens and chat IDs in package source
file_indicators: References to /DCIM and root directory scanning
network_indicators: Outbound connections to Telegram API from Python package code
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that contain import-time code in __init__.py which scans user directories and sends files to external endpoints, especially Telegram API. Flag packages with hardcoded bot tokens or chat IDs, and alert on unexpected outbound connections to api.telegram.org from development environments. Use static analysis to detect recursive os.walk usage combined with network exfiltration logic.
